_provenance_policy.why: Every published fee table we have found in this space is undated and uncited, which is why they silently rot. This corpus makes provenance a first-class field so a stale rate is visible rather than invisible.

source_tier.primary: Amazon Seller Central rate card or official policy page, read directly.
source_tier.secondary: Reputable third-party aggregator. Directionally reliable, NOT safe to quote to a paying client without primary confirmation.
source_tier.inferred: Derived from other fields in this corpus, not independently sourced.

_provenance_policy.rule: No figure carrying source_tier 'secondary' may appear in a client-facing deliverable until re-verified against primary and promoted. See VERIFY.md.

referral_fees._note: Amazon froze referral percentages for both 2025 and 2026. These are the most stable numbers in the corpus.
referral_fees._minimum_note: Applies to most categories. Some carry no minimum and some carry a higher one — per-category minimums are NOT yet captured here.

flat._shape: single rate applied to the whole sale price
flat._sports_and_outdoors_note: CONFIRMED primary 2026-08-19 via sell.amazon.com/pricing — flat 15%, no brackets, therefore no dead zone.

tiered._critical: Amazon runs TWO different tiered structures and distinguishes them only by wording on the rate card. Conflating them is the most common error in third-party fee calculators, and the reason this corpus separates them explicitly.

_modes.whole_price: One rate, selected by which bracket the total sales price lands in, then applied to the ENTIRE price. Rate-card tell: 'X% for products with a total sales price greater than $N'.
_modes.marginal: Each bracket's rate applies only to the portion of the price inside that bracket. Rate-card tell: 'X% for the portion of the total sales price up to $N'.

apparel._verbatim: 5% for products with a total sales price of $15.00 or less · 10% for products with a total sales price greater than $15.00 and less than or equal to $20.00 · 17% for products with a total sales price greater than $20.00
apparel._why_whole_price: Reads 'products with a total sales price', never 'portion of'. Contrast the jewelry row below, which is explicitly per-portion. The two rows in the same table use different language because they are different structures.
apparel._worked_example: A $10.00 shirt pays $0.50 (5% of the whole price), not the $1.70 a flat-17% model reports.
apparel._divergence_example: A $30.00 shirt: whole_price gives $5.10; marginal would give $3.45. The two modes disagree by $1.65 on one unit — which is why the mode, not the rates, is the thing to verify.

beauty_health_personal_care._verbatim: 8% for products with a total sales price of $10.00 or less, and 15% for items with a total sales price greater than $10.00
beauty_health_personal_care._why_it_matters: Hair accessories, including most headbands, classify here rather than under Clothing and Accessories. The Amazon browse department shown in search is NOT the referral category — this was found the hard way, by checking listings that a fashion-department search had returned.

baby_products._verbatim: 8% for products with a total sales price of $10.00 or less, and 15% for products with a total sales price greater than $10.00

grocery_and_gourmet._verbatim: 8% for products with a total sales price of $15.00 or less, and 15% for products with a total sales price greater than $15.00
grocery_and_gourmet._why_it_matters: The widest single dead zone we have found, and $15.99 — a ubiquitous price point in specialty food — sits inside it.

lawn_mowers_and_snow_throwers._verbatim: 15% for products with a total sales price of up to $500.00, and 8% for products with a total sales price greater than $500.00
lawn_mowers_and_snow_throwers._note: Rate DROPS above the boundary, so this is the inverse of a dead zone — crossing $500.00 increases net revenue by about $35. No leak; a cliff in the seller's favour.

furniture._verbatim: 15% for the portion of the total sales price up to $200.00, and 10% for any portion of the total sales price greater than $200.00

watches._verbatim: 16% for the portion of the total sales price up to $1,500.00, 3% for any portion of the total sales price greater than $1,500.00

appliances_compact._verbatim: 15% for the portion of the total sales price up to $300.00, and 8% for any portion of the total sales price greater than $300.00

electronics_accessories._verbatim: 15% for the portion of the total sales price up to $100.00, and 8% for any portion of the total sales price greater than $100.00

jewelry._verbatim: 20% for the portion of the total sales price up to $250.00, and 5% for any portion of the total sales price greater than $250.00
jewelry._worked_example: A $400.00 piece pays $50.00 + $7.50 = $57.50, not the $80.00 a flat-20% model reports.

_gaps: Per-category minimum referral fee overrides not captured.
Media closing fee (historically $1.80/unit on books, DVDs, music) not yet confirmed for 2026.
Categories charging above 20% (up to 45%) not enumerated.

fba_size_tiers._note: The tier boundary is where the money is. A carton a fraction of an inch over a threshold pays an entire tier more on every unit shipped, permanently, and almost no seller audits for it.
fba_size_tiers._evaluation_rule: Sort the three measured sides descending → longest, median, shortest. An item falls in the first tier whose every limit it satisfies. Shipping weight uses the greater of unit weight and dimensional weight where dim weight applies.

tiers.label: Small standard
tiers._boundary_note: The 0.75in shortest-side limit is the highest-yield boundary on Amazon. Poly-bagging instead of boxing, or trimming insert thickness, routinely moves a product from Large standard to Small standard.

tiers.label: Bulky (split into Small Bulky / Large Bulky on 2026-01-15)
tiers._note: Amazon split the former Large Bulky tier into Small Bulky and Large Bulky effective 2026-01-15. Exact dimensional boundaries for the split NOT yet captured — do not compute bulky-tier findings from this corpus.

_overmax.trigger: longest side over 96in, OR length + girth over 130in

fulfillment_fee_changes_2026._warning: Per-tier per-weight-band base fulfillment rates are NOT in this corpus yet. Only the 2026 deltas and surcharges below are captured. Do not compute an absolute fulfillment fee from this file.

reimbursement_policy._note: This is the outreach wedge. It is opt-in, most sellers have not done it, and it silently discounts every future claim they file.
reimbursement_policy._basis_note: Previously reimbursed at sale price. Manufacturing cost excludes shipping, handling, customs duties.

seller_declared_cost.where: Inventory Defect and Reimbursement portal → Manage Your Manufacturing Cost
seller_declared_cost.if_not_declared: Amazon substitutes its own estimate derived from comparable products.
seller_declared_cost._shortfall_confidence: secondary, widely repeated across seller-tooling vendors but not independently measured by us. Present as 'reported to run 20-30% low', never as a hard number.

auto_reimbursement.applies_to: items reported lost in a fulfillment center
auto_reimbursement._note: Amazon now issues these proactively. Recovery services retain value on discrepancies, complex transfers, and ambiguous warehouse events that automation misses.
